# Report usage across every tool round, not just the last

Issue: re-cinq/HALEngine#93
Labels: priority:medium, type:feature, size:S, area:api

## Why

`afterModelResponse` is the hook a deployer reaches for when they need to record what a turn cost — an audit entry, a billing line, a usage budget. It is called once per user message, after the round loop exits, and is handed the `lastUsage` local: `chatOrchestrator.ts` assigns `lastUsage = outcome.usage ?? lastUsage` on each round, so what the hook receives is the usage of the final provider call alone.

For a turn that answered directly, that is the whole turn. For a turn that called tools, it is the last leg of several, and the earlier rounds — including the one carrying the customer's question and the full tool results — are not counted anywhere. A deployer billing or budgeting from this hook under-counts exactly the expensive turns, and nothing in the signature hints at it. The current behaviour is recorded in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` so it is at least discoverable, but documenting a surprising number is weaker than not producing one.

Raised by the reviewer on HALEngine#83, which recorded the behaviour but could not change it: that PR's ticket scoped itself to specifying the seam, not altering the orchestrator.

## What to do

Decide, and make the signature say the answer. Two shapes are worth weighing, and the issue should record why the other was rejected:

- Accumulate across rounds and pass the sum, keeping one `usage` argument. Simple for the common case, and it silently changes what an existing consumer records — the number gets larger for tool-heavy turns, which is the point, but it is a behaviour change worth a MINOR bump and a changelog line that says so.
- Pass both, for example the summed total plus the per-round breakdown, so a consumer that wants provider-call granularity keeps it. More faithful, wider surface.

Whichever is chosen, a turn that ran no tools must report exactly what it reports today, so the common path does not move.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A turn driven through two tool rounds reports usage covering every provider call in that turn, asserted against a scripted provider whose rounds report known, different token counts
- [ ] A turn with no tool calls reports exactly what it reports today, pinned by the existing test remaining unedited
- [ ] A provider that reports no usage on some rounds does not make the total `undefined` or `NaN`: the rounds that reported are still counted, and a turn where nothing reported still reports nothing
- [ ] The type of what the hook receives makes the answer unambiguous, so a reader does not have to open the orchestrator to learn whether it is a sum
- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded under-counting line with the new behaviour, and the CHANGELOG entry states the change in what an existing consumer will record
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass, with no `any` in the public API

## Tech notes

Out of scope: the audit entry or billing record itself, which is a consumer's concern; token accounting for anything other than the provider calls the orchestrator makes; and the `stop` chunk's own `usage` shape, which providers already populate and this issue only aggregates.

Key files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `lastUsage` local and the `afterModelResponse` call site), `src/types/ai.ts` (`UsageMetadata`), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.

# Definition of Done

> `afterModelResponse` is the hook a deployer reaches for when they need to record what a turn cost — an audit entry, a billing line, a usage budget. It is called once per user message, after the round loop exits, and is handed the `lastUsage` local: `chatOrchestrator.ts` assigns `lastUsage = outcome.usage ?? lastUsage` on each round, so what the hook receives is the usage of the final provider call alone.

**Strategy: `direct`** — The orchestrator hook `afterModelResponse` is directly observable through the `chatOrchestrator` factory and a mock provider seam, allowing us to assert the accumulated usage.

## Done when these pass

- [ ] **reports usage covering every provider call in a multi-round turn** — validates that the hook receives the accumulated sum of token usage across all provider rounds
  `src/orchestration/turn-usage.acceptance.test.ts`
- [ ] **accumulates usage safely when some rounds report no usage** — validates that rounds with missing usage don't corrupt the accumulated total
  `src/orchestration/turn-usage.acceptance.test.ts`

## Facets

- [x] Update `chatOrchestrator.ts` to sum the usage across rounds instead of keeping only `lastUsage`
- [x] Introduce a type alias like `TurnUsageMetadata` for the hook parameter to make the accumulated nature unambiguous
- [x] Add a CHANGELOG entry stating the change in what an existing consumer will record

## Out of scope

- the audit entry or billing record itself, which is a consumer's concern
- token accounting for anything other than the provider calls the orchestrator makes
- the `stop` chunk's own `usage` shape, which providers already populate and this issue only aggregates

19:- **`afterModelResponse` now receives the accumulated sum of every provider call in the turn**, not only the last round's usage. A hook that records billing or audit data from this field previously counted only the last round for tool-heavy turns; it now counts every round. The type of the third parameter is `TurnUsageMetadata` (exported from the package root, structurally identical to `UsageMetadata`) to make the per-turn accumulation explicit. **Migration note**: if your `afterModelResponse` hook used the usage value as a proxy for the last provider call alone, it now receives a larger number — the total for the whole turn. A turn that ran no tools is unchanged. A turn where every provider call reported no usage still reports `undefined`, not a zero-filled object.
40:- `HalEngineConfig.transport` now accepts three optional extension points: `additionalRoutes` (mounts a router under `basePath`, unauthenticated), `rootRoutes` (mounts a router at `/`, after the `basePath` router and before the 404 catch-all), and `errorHandler` (replaces Express's default HTML error page). Pass none of them and the app is identical to before. See `docs/getting-started.md` for usage and the GDPR / NIS-2 notes that apply to unauthenticated routes.
42:- `OrchestratorHooks` gains an optional `onToolBudgetExhausted(session, budget)` hook, and `ToolBudgetInfo` (`{maxToolRounds, requestedTools}`) and `TOOL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` are exported. It fires when the model asks for a tool round `maxToolRounds` refuses, after the last provider call and before `afterModelResponse`. Return a sentence and the turn ends on it as an ordinary assistant entry, so the user sees a degraded answer instead of silence; the engine writes no prose of its own. Every exhausted run now also ends with a `{type: 'stop', stopReason: 'tool_budget_exhausted'}` chunk, a new value for the existing field rather than a new type, which the WebSocket transport sends nothing for. The turn still ends with `stream_end`, never `error`. Additive: with no hook installed, the wire is unchanged.
54:- The WebSocket server no longer echoes the access token in its handshake response. A client offers the new `hal.v1` marker beside its token (`new WebSocket(url, ['hal.v1', token])`, or `HAL_WS_SUBPROTOCOL`, now exported from the package root) and the server answers only `hal.v1`, so the token stays out of the 101 response headers and off the connected socket's `protocol` property. The token is read as the first offered value that is not the marker, in either order, and still reaches tools as `authHeaders.authorization`. `credentialFromSubprotocol`, also newly exported, reads it the same way for your own `WsAuthenticator`. **Migration note**: every client must be updated to offer `hal.v1` alongside its token, and an authenticator that took the first `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` value as the token now gets `hal.v1` from an updated client, so read it with `credentialFromSubprotocol(req.headers['sec-websocket-protocol'])` instead. From the next MINOR, a client that offers only a bare token receives a 101 with no `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` header, and `ws` and Chromium both fail such a handshake; this release still accepts a bare token (see Deprecated), because `0.2.x` documented it.
58:- Offering a bare access token as the only WebSocket subprotocol. This release still echoes it and logs a warning that never includes the offered value; the next MINOR stops echoing it, and a client that has not added `hal.v1` will then fail its handshake.
